label: Aquamarine, Paris Cavanagh choreography
review: The script was over-packed at 116% density, causing lines to overlap each other and talk over key vocal cues and the bass drop. We dropped surplus transition callouts and merged overlapping phrases so every texture shift, signature hair whip, tutting hit, and floorwork pose lands cleanly on the music with room to breathe. The script captures the piece's signature hair whips, tutting, and floorwork well, but several floorwork and final-phrase cues land a second after the movement initiates, the suspenseful wide-stance isolation before the first bass drop is vague, and the 49s fold callout is too wordy before the groove.

label: Track 10, Paris Cavanagh choreography
review: The script mislabeled commercial waacking and flamenco-inspired wrist rolls as 'Bharatanatyam frames' and 'mudra-like shapes', and its 98% speech density left no breathing room for the music. Tightening the phrasing and shifting slow descriptions to brisk pacing fixes the style terminology, lands callouts on the hits, and lets the track breathe between phrases. The script captures the structure well, but 'Heavy bass:' at 12.5s reads like a director's note rather than dance narration, several callouts (16.4s, 27.4s) land slightly late against the hits, and key leg/arm specifics—the wide second-position plié at 4.4s, the bound arm wrap at 8.8s, the knee hitch at 17.0s, and the side attitude unfolding into the 21s extension—need sharper technical language.

label: The Royal Family: HHI NZ megacrew, 1st place 2019
style: commercial hip-hop megacrew choreography with dancehall, femme/jazz-funk, and acrobatic stunt influences
review: The script was at 95% density, talking non-stop over key vocal hooks ('It's Britney, bitch', 'Gimme the Light', 'Sally Walker') and colliding across section transitions. I dropped surplus transition lines to let the music breathe and re-timed late callouts (such as the 135 s bow and 'YAK!' fist pumps, the 73 s starburst frame, and the 113 s vogue dip) so every signature megacrew illusion, stunt, and texture change lands on the beat. At 79% density, the script talks almost continuously and causes back-to-back line collisions during the fast formations (73–98 s, 114–122 s, and 167–179 s) while talking over key vocal hooks ('YAWK!', 'It's Britney, bitch'). Dropping surplus transition lines and tightening overlapping callouts lets the music and spoken-word breaks breathe while keeping every signature megacrew illusion, costume contrast, and groove shift sharp on the beat.

label: NJ Center of Dance: Vogue (studio piece, 2022)
style: studio commercial jazz with vogue influences
review: The script was far too dense at 89%, talking over key vocal hooks and repeating the ending trio freeze twice. Several lines also misdescribed movements or arrived late, including calling the soloist's cartwheel into a high kick a 'cartwheel drop', hallucinating face frames during the diagonal spire reach at 25 s, and starting the soloist's straddle-split line late. The script was too dense at 73% speech, crowding the music, and several callouts in the climax landed late after the moves had already happened. I also corrected the final trio pose (they stand in sassy hip-cocked bevels with hands at their chins, rather than lunging in), tightened wordy lines, and cut three surplus lines to let the beat drops breathe.

label: Usha Jey: Hybrid Bharatham, episode 5 ("Uproar")
review: At 110% density, the script talked non-stop over key vocal hooks and overlapped itself; it also misdescribed the 24.3s street-style knee hop as a turned-out Anjali jump, missed the diagonal arm slashes at 15s, and mislabelled the 30s synchronized mudra switches as a canon. Trimming surplus callouts and tightening lines gives the trap beat and rap cues room to breathe while sharpening the Bharatanatyam-hip-hop fusion details. The script was too dense (80%), causing several lines to collide (6.2s into 8.8s, 18.9s into 21.5s, 26.3s into 29.9s, and 41.4s into 43.3s) and leaving little room for the rap track to breathe. I dropped two surplus lines, tightened phrasing and timing to land on the hits (including the final freeze before the 78.2s fade-out), and replaced unexplained Sanskrit squat terms with clear visual descriptions while highlighting the single-file multi-armed illusion.

label: Prix de Lausanne 2026, Dayeon Yeom: classical variation
review: The script is far too dense at 91% speech, talking over the music through repeated phrases, and gets several technical details and timings wrong: at 15 s her left foot (not right) is pointed front in croisé, the arabesque descriptions at 51.9 s and 56.8 s are two seconds late (spoken during the attitude toe-taps after the arabesques have already finished), and the turns at 59 s are en dehors pirouettes from a fourth-position lunge rather than piqué turns. Trimming redundant repeat lines and tightening phrasing lets the orchestra breathe while keeping every signature tambourine accent, balance, and turn crisp and on beat. Several steady descriptions were too long and dragged into the next movement or over the music, and a few lines missed exact ballet terminology (échappé to second, rising rather than springing onto pointe for the tambourine kicks) or landed slightly late on the attitude balance and grand jeté.

label: Prix de Lausanne 2023, Ana Luisa Negrão: contemporary
review: The script was overly dense (81%), repeating the entrance description and talking over the music during phrasing transitions, while mislabeling several key moves: the figure-four balance into a back penché at 57.8 s was called a vertical tilt, the doll-like heel pops at 113 s were missed, the alternating left-right-left 180-degree tilts at 121.8 s had the wrong direction, and the dive into a center split at 130 s was described as sliding on the diagonal. The script over-narrates at 79% density (talking over the solo violin entrance and final piano chord), mislabels parallel or crossed bent knees as 'second-position plié' and 'crossed plié' at 62.2 s and 118.2 s, and is several seconds late on key moments including the figure-four balance (56 s), past-vertical tilt (98 s), center split (128 s), and curtain-call bow (150.5 s).

label: Eleganza Waacking Festival 2023: Team Korea
review: At 79% speech density, the narration was talking non-stop over the disco track; dropping surplus transition lines lets the music and horn hits breathe. Fixed the mischaracterized 27 s vocal swell (a slow, sensual head caress, not a rapid arm whip) and sharpened technical detail on the one-legged passé balance in heels and the final split and stag leaps. The script is slightly too dense (60%) and crowds key vocal entrances and the final freeze, with a few cues arriving a beat after the movement starts (the opening horn strut at 17.8 s, the right-wing solo at 122.8 s, and the high-kick climax at 169.8 s). Dropping three transitional lines gives the disco vocals and horn build-ups room to breathe, while tightening the remaining lines and merging the final two cues lets every hit land squarely on the music.

label: Sadeck: Murmuration (tutting)
review: The script was over-packed at 107% density, leaving no room for the music and making the rapid geometric shapes hard to picture with eyes closed. I dropped the crowded line at 26.2s, tightened every line so the bass drops and snare rolls breathe, highlighted the signature contrast of bare forearms against black clothing, and named the leader's conducting illusion and finger-tutting solo. The script was far too dense (90% speech), with long steady lines bleeding into the next musical phrase and overwhelming the listener with nonstop shape names. Tightening lines to a brisk pace and establishing the front leader at the start gives the listener one clear geometric image at a time while leaving breathing room for the beat drops.

label: IndianRaga: Vahana Alarippu
review: The script was far too dense (89% speech), talking continuously over the rhythmic vocal percussion (solkattu) with duplicate lines (76.8s/80.9s, 97.4s/100.5s, 116.6s/120.4s) and ballet terms ('plié') instead of Bharatanatyam terminology. I cut surplus and repetitive lines to let the mridangam and vocal calls breathe, tightened phrasing, and clarified the piece's signature multi-armed deity illusions and vahana (mount) tableaux. The script captures the multi-armed deity tableaux and neck isolations well, but misses the piece's Vahana Alarippu concept (deities and their sacred animal mounts), uses 'tiptoe' where the dancers use classical heel-toe gliding steps or rise onto the balls of the feet, and mistimes several transitions (the 59.8s stamp callout, the 98.5s squat bounces and heel-kick jumps, the 109.2s charioteer walk, the 121.5s role-swap spin, and the 174.5s orbit into the final hops). Tightening wordy lines also gives the vocal konnakol percussion room to breathe.

One kneels; behind her, the other spins with buoyant bent-knee hops.
Spinning to swap places, they stack as a four-armed deity.
Split into low heel extension and high arch, then sweep arms across.
Tandem crossed-ankle pose, arms opposing, then turning in.
In aramandi, crossed hands crown one; the other glides her neck, turning.
One steps in a wide arc, wrists rolling, as her partner stamps in place.
Side-by-side unison: sharp wrist sweeps snap into wide horizontal arms!
Pivoting with backs turned, palms joined in deep squats, stamping.
Spinning to an upright freeze, palms pressed in Anjali mudra.
Orbiting back-to-back, they swap sides, hopping with left arm arched high!

label: Rocío Garrido: soleá
review: The script was too dense (79%), talking over the singer's emotional vocal cries and the rhythmic footwork with repetitive lines about 'floreo', 'heavy ruffled train', and 'hunched in profile'. I dropped redundant lines to let the guitar, palmas, and cante breathe, corrected the 31.8 s move (an arm release into an over-the-shoulder glare, not a train kick) and the 172.2 s phrasing ('coiling the train into a high overhead frame'), and tightened late callouts at 121.0 s, 152.0 s, and 171.2 s to land cleanly on the hits. The script captures the flamenco vocabulary well, but at 63% density it talks over the singer's raw vocal entrances (cante) and stacks back-to-back callouts that collide during fast turns and remates. Dropping overlapping setup lines lets the cante and guitar breathe, while tightening and shifting several late lines ensures the train kicks, arm changes, and profile freezes land right on the beat.
signature: heavy, sweeping manipulation of the black ruffled bata de cola train: legs, feet, and lower torso
statuesque overhead arm frames with intricate finger fanning: arms, wrists, and fingers
sharp, percussive footwork calls that lock into sudden profile freezes: feet, torso, and head

lines.text: Bailaora sweeps in, settling facing the musicians with elbows rounded.
Sharp heel kick fans her bata de cola train!
With her back to us, she holds a tense, still pose, arms poised slightly out from her sides.
She twists slowly to look over her shoulder, back arched, framing her sorrowful gaze.
With one arm curved overhead, she glares forward, then snaps her arms open wide.
Sudden drop, slicing arms wide as the ruffles flare!
Holds a fierce splayed-hand pose, then erupts into explosive llamada stamps!
Pivoting turn—a heel kick whips her heavy train wide.
Hunched in profile, she lifts her skirt and stamps crisp zapateado heels.
Spinning in place, a whipping turn kicks the heavy train flying!
Arms shoot high, arched taut for the cante!
Fists unclench; right arm falls suddenly to her hip as her left fans high.
Rolling wrists frame her face, then reach to the right with an intense expression.
A whipping vuelta kicks the heavy train airborne, arms framing her head!
Holds a deep back arch, then kicks the train and spins right.
Steps slowly forward, fingers splayed low as her hips sway.
Hunched heel-flicks build into rapid turns, whipping the train in a wide orbit.
Spins twice whipping her train—machine-gun footwork, slashing arms down!
Reversing her spin, she kicks the train into a deep quiebro backbend!
From sharp footwork, a high train kick spins into an arched pose!
Kicks the train aside, standing facing upstage with taut, splayed hands.
Whips front, coiling the train beside her.
Left arm high, right arm framing her torso with fluid floreo wrist circles.

label: Amapiano Dance Championship: Gugulethu United We Stand Dancers
review: The script was far too dense (78%), with back-to-back lines talking over vocal breaks, duplicate lines in the intro and middle sections, and a hallucinated knee-pulse line at 137s where the dancers are actually upright kicking. Dropping redundant lines and tightening key transitions lets the Amapiano log drum and vocal cues breathe while clarifying the footwork and heist staging. Fixed a hallucinated squat at 119s (they are upright hopping and kicking to the chants, while the wide-stance knee-knock squat actually hits at 137s) and added the center leader standing tall above the final floor freeze at 162s. Tightened callouts, fixed the late huddle timing at 80.5s, and dropped redundant lines at 42.5s and 130.5s so the music can breathe.
signature: Bank Heist theatrical framing with masks and props: whole body posture, hands holding signs, masks, and loot bag
Synchronized deep squat drops and level changes: legs, hips, and knees dropping sharply toward the floor
Wide-stance bent-knee rapid legwork: knees, hips, and ankles with torso pitched forward

lines.text: Amapiano theatre: two dancers walk in from opposite wings, signs held high.
Walking inward to meet at center, holding signs reading Bank Heist overhead.
Two masked dancers in red jumpsuits stalk in from the wings.
Sign-holders flank the stage as one dancer struts forward, briefcase in hand.
Far right drops into a lookout crouch while others tilt masked heads.
Briefcase down, masks pushed up—they drop into a wide crouch!
Deep squat drop, springing up with wide arm extensions!
Double-bounce squat, springing into cross-body kicks!
Wide-stance bounce circling one arm high, then hop-flicking the right leg.
Huddling tight, they hurdle-leap wide and drop down!
Drop to one knee, then split into clusters, hunching with bouncing knees.
Spreading wide, hinged forward with hands on thighs, torsos bounce sharply.
Upright on the chants, feet shuffle crisp and fast as fists pump down.
Stage floods magenta; in wide stances, they lean and pump elbows.
Wide-stance side steps, flinging arms open then punching one hand high.
Drop to touch the floor, then snap into a wide stance, right arms reaching out!
Bouncing through upright footwork, they drop wide, pumping one knee in!
Drop low into right lunges, then bounce stepping side-to-side.
Bouncy heel-tap footwork across the stage, center dancer folding low.
Bouncing on one leg, they drive sharp knee lifts and low kicks!
Arms punch high, then all crash to hands and knees!

label: HomeBros: Afro dance choreography
review: At 85% density the narration crowds out the Afrobeats groove, and in the finale it confuses the dancer in glasses with the original center dancer after they swap places. I dropped ten transitional lines to let the music breathe, fixed the leg-fanning mechanics at 55.2 s and wave-to-tick order at 86.5 s, and clarified the dancer in glasses leading the climax. The script captures the contrast of the big dancer's featherlight footwork and the trio's heavy unison well, but misses the center dancer's theatrical face-framing hand hits at 62s, is late on the bucket-hat soloist's liquid wave at 85.5s and the final bow at 149s, and has a few wordy or ambiguous lines.
signature: Contrast of size and agility: the largest dancer (in glasses) executing ultra-fast, light-footed swivels and high-energy hops with effortless precision.: Feet, ankles, knees, and hips

Explosive trio unison: three dancers of very different body types locking into identical low-center-of-gravity grooves and synchronized jumps.: Full body, especially deep knee bends (pliés) and torso leans
Playful, theatrical facial expressions and crowd engagement paired with sharp isolated hits.: Face, head, shoulders, and hands

lines.text: Three men in black take the floor; one brushes his chest.
Three dancers line up; center dips into a wide-knee bounce.
Face each other, then bounce forward, right hands hovering overhead.
Two step back; right dancer solos, sliding a foot out, pumping knees.
Loose footwork into a sharp right-knee lift, stepping down to lean back!
Trio hits unison with springy knee lifts and crossed-foot bounces.
Drop wide, hands on knees, rolling heads slowly across!
Sinking wide, they roll hips and shoulders, then pivot left to hop.
Right arms shoot skyward, quarter-turning into a low bounce!
Arms cross and slice open; shoulders shimmy in wide stances.
Hinged forward, arms dangling, they kick-step side to side.
Deep squat drop, rebounding wide into a tilted shoulder roll!
They step and bounce together, pumping raised hands forward on the beat!
Feet together, he glides right on rapid heel-toe swivels, hands on thighs.
Alternating high-knee lifts across the body, arms relaxed!
Bouncing on one foot, he drives high knees, then turns into a wide crouch.
Bucket-hat soloist tilts his head, hitches a knee, and ticks his wrists.
A liquid wave ripples through his arms into robotic ticks overhead.
Spinning front, he hops high, tapping ankles and knees!
Still hold, then explosive left leg shoot into bouncy knee lifts!
Bouncy knee lifts, crossing arms, then rolling wrists overhead.
Trio locks into a heavy wide groove, two whipping right arms overhead.
The dancer in glasses kicks side, punching down into chest hits.
Freezes, hand to mouth in mock shock!
Reaching forward, all three explode into wide side-to-side hops!
High knees driving, forearms rolling!
Arms wide, he glides on weightless heel-toe swivels, then hops into a low run.
Center dancer pivots on heel and toe, all three grooving with raised palms.
Spinning to face front, the centre dancer bows as partners clap.

label: Javi & Alice: 1st place salsa cabaret couples, ULDC 2017
review: The script had a duplicate line at 92.4s/92.7s, confused stage and viewer left/right at 78.5s–82.4s, misdescribed the final shoulder-wrap spin at 130.5s as 'legs pressed tight' when she is in a wide V-split, and was late on the floor split (27.8s), waist spins (108.5s), and both climactic lifts (124.2s, 130.5s, 136.5s). I tightened the timing to land on the movements, corrected the technical shapes, and dropped surplus lines so the salsa groove and brass hits can breathe. Several climax and signature lines were timed 1.5 to 2.5 seconds late—most notably the waist-assisted spins (starting at 107.7 s, not 108.5 s), the two final horizontal rotational lifts (starting at 122.0 s and 129.0 s, not 124.2 s and 130.5 s), and the final floor leg mount and freeze (which finishes on the 136.5 s chord rather than starting there). Repetitive partner-turn lines at 87.5 s and 104.8 s were dropped and the 38.0 s/41.2 s lift sequence consolidated so the narration stays on beat and lets the salsa vocals and mambo horns breathe.
signature: High-velocity horizontal rotational lifts where the woman's body is cantilevered straight out from the man's torso as he pivots: full body — the man's core and legs anchoring the pivot while the woman holds a rigid horizontal line or wide split through her hips and legs
Extreme flexibility lines integrated into partner transitions — full front splits on the floor, vertical standing leg extensions, and wide straddle jumps: hips, legs, and pointed feet
Blurringly fast waist-assisted spins on one foot with the free leg tucked at the knee: woman's supporting foot, spotting head, and core, driven by the man's hands on her waist
Side-by-side unison salsa shines with sharp ribcage shimmies and syncopated kicks facing the audience: feet, knees, hips, shoulders, and ribcage

sections.label: Dramatic brass intro with floor drop and acrobatic lifts
First salsa verse: partnerwork, shines, and shoulder-sit lift
Mambo/montuno section: travelling kicks, unison shines, and rapid waist-assisted spins

sections.label: Climactic rotational lifts and final pose

lines.text: A salsa cabaret pair walks onstage together from the right.
Stacked in a taut freeze: toe pointed, his left arm high.
From their opening pose, he spins her sharply out.
High fan kick into an arched split-leg shoulder spin!
From a standing split, he hoists her onto his shoulder in splits!
Set down from vertical split into playful chest shimmies.
Midair straddle split at his waist!
Lifted straddle split, then partner turns; she ducks between his legs.
In shadow hold, rippling body waves and overhead reach, then side-stepping hip grooves.
Tangled two-hand wraps whip her through rapid, continuous partner spins.
High leg extension to her ear!
She kicks high, then leaps into a tall shoulder sit!
She slides down his front into unison high kicks.
She slices a high front kick as he frames her from behind.
He kicks high, then both spin out into solo footwork.
Overhead lead, he drives blurring one-foot spins, free leg hooked!
In shadow position, rolling rumba shoulders melt into grounded sideways steps.
Sharp hop together, then crisp heel-toe taps, right arms punching high!
He scoops her into a fast hip-spin lift, back arched!
He lifts her inverted across his chest, spinning her in a straddle!
Lowered to the floor, she shoots one leg vertical as he poses.

label: Tap Dance World Championship 2012: adult male solo
review: At 93% speech density, the narration talks almost continuously over the tap acoustics and UK garage beat, drowning out the very rhythms the dancer is making. I dropped surplus filler lines to let the tap breaks breathe, tightened wordy descriptions into punchy, in-meter commentary, and aligned timestamps and details (like the fist snap at 26s, the side-to-side leaps at 111s, and the machine-gun rolls at 126.5s) to land right on the hits. Several lines were 2 to 5 seconds late—most notably the heart-clutch mime at 19.8 s, the lunge freeze and spins at 67–68 s, the crouched forearm-pumping groove at 78–83 s, and the machine-gun rolls at the floor mics at 126 s—and the 74 s windmilling hops into the 76.2 s attitude toe-tip balance were missed. Tightening verbose lines and realigning timestamps locks the commentary to the hits while leaving room to hear the tap rhythms.
signature: Single-leg backward hopping while the free leg brushes the floor and both arms windmill backward: Legs, feet, and full-arm circles
Crossed-ankles toe-stand balances and sliding crossovers with arms stretched wide like a tightrope walker: Feet (tips of tap shoes), crossed legs, wide-open arms
Crouched, bent-knee profile groove traveling sideways with rhythmic forearm pumps and backward arm swings: Bent knees, pitched-forward torso, forearms, and feet
High-flung loose arms and wide-open chest during airborne pullbacks, wings, and leg kicks: Arms, shoulders, and jumping legs

sections.label: Up-tempo Beat Drop and Rhythm Footwork

lines.text: Solo tapper in a grey vest jogs easy to center stage.
Facing upstage, he adjusts his vest and waits in quiet focus.
Pivots to profile on a heel-toe tap, flicking one foot out.
Sweeps arms wide, whipping into vest-flaring tap spins!
Profile freeze, open palm rising slowly in yearning.
Crossed-ankle toe stand, wobbling with tightrope arms wide.
Turns and leans forward, scuffing one foot back with wide-swinging arms.
Sharp freeze, gazing right; then grins, kicking into crisp heel-toe taps.
Turns to profile, hopping as free leg kicks back and arms swing.
Hops with swinging back kicks, then rapid cross-foot shuffles and whip turn!
Crisp heel-toe taps, then wide-flung hops kicking side to side!
Kicks into a slick, moonwalk-style heel-toe backslide.
Rapid tap crossovers into a wide split freeze, palm pressed out!
Spins into buoyant hops, kicking heels up behind with arms wide!
Suspended toe-tip balance, back leg hooked high, arms reaching!
Crouched in profile, swinging arms overhead into rapid tap shuffles.
Crisp heel-toe taps and jumps, then a one-legged hopping turn, arms high.
Side-glance pause, then buoyant crossing tap steps, arms wide.
Double wing jumps—scraping both feet mid-air, arms flung wide!
Arms hugged to his chest, whipping through rapid spins.
Arms shoot wide, balancing on the side edges of crossed tap shoes.
Buoyant leaps and sharp claps, clicking heels mid-air with wide arms!
High hopping wings, scraping mid-air with arms flung wide!
Rapid tap footwork, then hopping right, kicking heels back with swinging arms.
Pitched over the mics in rapid heel-toe rolls, rising to groove.
Final stamp on the stop, strolling casually upstage.

label: Ascendance Studio Company: "Trolls" (studio recital, 2022)
review: At 83% speech density, the narration talked almost nonstop over the tap rhythms and chorus hooks; dropping redundant repeat lines gives the music and footwork room to breathe. Several directional and movement errors were also fixed, including reversing left and right at 48.5 s and 116.2 s, fixing late timing on the 25 s clap and 95 s hair whips, and removing a hallucinated turn at 128.0 s. The script is too dense (65%), with several redundant or colliding lines, a late call on the double clap at 24.7 s, and an inaccurate 'two lines' description at 35.2 s (they remain in a single line viewed in perspective from the side camera). Tightening and merging adjacent phrases gives the music room to breathe while fixing the timing, highlighting the close-up footwork at 80.5 s, and catching the crossed-arm groove at 111.8 s.
signature: Playful character gestures highlighting the tall pink Troll wigs, including patting the hair and whipping the wigs in circles: head, hair, and arms
Unison beginner tap footwork—shuffles, toe taps, and heel digs—performed in a single horizontal line with hands on hips: feet, ankles, and legs with torso upright and hands on hips
Bent-knee forward lean with hands on knees and rhythmic hip/shoulder bounces: hips, knees, and torso

lines.text: Nine young tappers in sparkly blue and tall pink Troll wigs, hands on hips.
Hands on hips, unison shuffle-steps, pink wigs bobbing.
Pivoting to the side, bouncing with bent elbows pumping!
Double clap, then hit poses with arms in Vs!
Turning side, arms sweep high, then one reaches forward, one overhead.
Facing front, arms tilt diagonally with a low flexed-foot kick.
Hands braced on knees, they crouch with heads dropped.
Up, rolling forearms at their chests over bouncy step-taps!
V-arms drop to hips; turning left, crisp tap steps in place.
Hands on hips for toe-heel taps, then wide stance with a wave.
Hands on hips for high marches, then hinge to bounce shoulders.
Hands on hips; close on feet lifting into sharp right heel digs.
Hands on knees, bouncing hips, then right dancer pops open!
Wide stance, hands on knees, whipping tall pink wigs in wild circles!
Rising from the crouch in canon, arms opening wide into a bounce.
Flexed wrists out, wiggling hips; hands clasp back for heel digs.
Marching forward, then bending with hands on knees to nod their wigs!
Hands on hips, they step forward and pump their shoulders.
One last big circular hair-whip, then stepping into ending poses.

label: WDSF World Open Prague: Standard final, waltz
review: At 92% density, the script talked over nearly every bar of the waltz ballad and repeated 'arched far back' and 'high toes' on almost every line; it also hallucinated a leg lift at 101.8 s, misidentified a turn as an oversway at 30.2 s and 58.0 s, and placed the final curtsy line at 140.4 s where it gets cut off. I trimmed surplus transitional lines to let the vocals and piano breathe, merged split descriptions into cohesive phrases capturing the pendulum swing and suspension, fixed the inaccuracies, and pulled the final curtsy line earlier. The script missed the purple-gowned follower's standout promenade développé at 62 s and mislabelled the side-by-side right lunges at 44.5 s as throwaway oversways. It also talked over too much of the slow waltz ballad (63% density), so several lines are tightened and surplus lines at 68.5 s, 106.8 s, and 120.5 s are dropped to let the piano and vocals breathe.
signature: Extreme arched upper-body shape and head weight in the female partners: Head, neck, upper spine, and ribcage
Pendulum swing and lofty suspension at the top of the rise: Knees, ankles, feet, and full-body center of mass
Sharp head snaps between closed and promenade positions: Head and eyes

lines.text: International Standard Slow Waltz; dancers wait poised on the parquet.
He opens his left arm; in pink feathers, she steps toward him.
From a breathed back-arch, a deep knee bend drives a pendulum turn onto high toes.
Gliding across the floor, opening into a sweeping back arch.
In black, a suspended arch rises into a quick spin turn.
Center, two couples sink into deep, arched oversway lunges.
The ombre gown whips through continuous pivots, skirt flaring wide.
In purple, a deep throwaway oversway rises into a high-reaching line.
Close in silver, a sweeping head roll rises into promenade.
Spinning in closed hold, she arches back as he extends a leg.
In pink feathers, she arches deep, then sweeps into promenade.
Slow turn in closed hold, sinking into an arched lunge.
In pink feathers, they glide in and rise onto high toes.
In purple, a tall suspended arch releases into fast, flaring pivots!
Underarm turn into a deep back-arched lunge, then rising to release.
She spins out; both stand tall, arms sweeping wide.
